ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized representatives against the South African Treasury Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, HM Treasury consolidated list, and the Financial Action Task Force High-Risk Jurisdictions list. FICA requires enhanced due diligence (EDD) for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), immediate family members and close associates, with an adequate risk-based CDD process, source of funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring for Amazon Pay and Stripe payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eServices portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must consist of printable alphanumeric characters in the Latin/Roman script. Names in any of the 11 official languages of South Africa are allowed; non-Roman script names (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into a standard Latin alphabet form. CIPC systems may reject names containing symbols, diacritics, or unidentifiable characters outside the approved ASCII range.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Incorporated (unless it is a valid legal-form indicator)
Limited (unless used in the approved form of liability)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may apply in writing to CIPC for administrative reconsideration within 15 business days of the notice, citing the relevant section of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulations, 2011. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file a formal appeal to the Companies Tribunal within 30 days of the reconfirmation, supported by written submissions and/or an application for condonation. Alternatively, the applicant may retry with a substantially transformed name immediately via the CIPC eServices portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or co-working office is acceptable for a low-risk standard-sector company provided it maintains a physical street address in South Africa that is open to the public during normal business hours and cannot be a Post Office box. A mail-forwarding-only address is not compliant. For the stated Montessori wooden blocks business using third-party logistics, a managed physical office with administrative support is considered permissible at incorporation, but the company should later maintain local books, minutes, and board decision records to evidence commercial substance for SARS and AML/CFT purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% to 15% probability of a documented physical compliance inspection in the first 12 months. The risk is elevated where the registered office is a bare virtual mailbox or the company is wholly foreign-owned with no local operational footprint. CIPC, the Financial Intelligence Centre, and the South African Police Service may conduct unannounced inspections, but for a low-risk Standard tier industry, annual proactive inspections are rare; cannabis, financial services, and high-risk dealers may expect much higher rates.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A) read together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1B)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital prescribed; no escrow account or capital duty requirement. The Memorandum of Incorporation may authorize 100 or more ordinary no-par or R1-par shares, and subscription proceeds must be paid into a South African bank account of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation of ZA Pty Ltd (Registration No. pending) under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 is hereby ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the founding subscribers subscribe to the ordinary shares set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation, with subscription consideration credited in full to the company's bank account. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the registered office be and remains at [registered address], South Africa, and any relocation be subject to board approval. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT [Name] be and is appointed Managing Director, [Name] be and is appointed Financial Director, and each consents to act. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Managing Director be authorized to effect all statutory filings and banking instructions. All resolutions are effective from signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and verify availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a company name search on the CIPC database and submit Form CoR 9.1 (Request for Reservation of a Company Name) with preferred names in order, accompanied by the identification details of the incorporator. The reservation is valid for 60 business days and the incorporation filing must be made within this period.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1
Identity document or passport of the incorporator
Proof of name search result
Payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as to be confusingly similar or contrary to public order, file alternative names in order of preference; respond to CIPC comments within 20 business days or the reservation lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation documents and obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services online portal / CIPC Customer Contact Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Form CoR 14.1A (Notice of Incorporation) and attach the signed Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1B) stating authorised share rights, director provisions, and registered office particulars. Submit electronically through CIPC e-Services and pay the prescribed registration fee. CIPC evaluates the documents and issues a Certificate of Incorporation and registration number.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1A (Notice of Incorporation)
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1B)
Name reservation certificate / proof of name reservation
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query or rejection, withdraw and re-file corrected incorporation documents within 10 business days; pay applicable re-filing fee; if the name is defamatory or negatively affects goodwill, lodge an objection with CIPC under Companies Act regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint initial directors and adopt registered office governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ZA Pty Ltd board and CIPC corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass written resolutions; formally appoint the Managing Director and Financial Director, record consent to act on Form CoR 14.1, and confirm the registered office address as required by section 23 of the Companies Act. Evidence of consents and the registered address must be retained in the company's statutory records and, if changed, filed with CIPC on Form CoR 14.1 for notice of registered office change.
required_dossiers: Written consent to act as director forms
Minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting
Memorandum of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is disqualified or refuses to act, nominate an alternate director, update the board resolution, and file amended consent forms with CIPC; if the registered office is unoccupied or invalid, file notice of change of address promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, VAT, PAYE and labour levy accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Department of Employment and Labour (DEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an income tax number via SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch; determine VAT registration threshold (compulsory from R1 million supply turnover; voluntary application from R50,000). Register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL if employees will be hired, and register with the Compensation Fund for COIDA coverage. All registrations must be supported by the incorporation certificate.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' identity documents or passports
Company bank account details
Registered address and trading address particulars
Anticipated number of employees and payroll information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS denies or queries the tax registration, correct the financial or identity information and re-submit via SARS eFiling; if penalties are imposed for late registration, apply for a remission of penalty under the Tax Administration Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal trading license and environmental compliance screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality (Business Licensing Authority) and Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the competent municipal authority for a business/trading license authorising the manufacturing and wholesale supply of educational toys at the identified premises. For the toy manufacturing activity, screen under the National Environmental Management Act (NEMA) 2004 Listing Notices; submit a DFFE screening report if required and obtain a waste handling registration if disposal of waste is anticipated. Secure fire clearance and occupational health and safety inspection evidence.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and board resolution
Premises zoning certificate / lease agreement
Fire safety certificate issued by municipal fire services
DFFE screening report (if triggered)
Toy product safety conformity evidence (EN71 / SANS 8128-compatible)
Occupational Health and Safety Act compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is refused due to zoning non-compliance, apply for a special zoning consent or seek alternative premises; if the DFFFE screening requires a Basic Assessment, appoint an independent Environmental Assessment Practitioner and submit the Basic Assessment Report for public participation and decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality (Business Licensing Authority) together with relevant provincial economic development and health and safety bodies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business/Trading License under the Business Licensing Act 24 of 1996 and municipal by-laws; a manufacturing permit may be required under the National Building Regulations for factory premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or low-impact Registration for beechwood toy manufacturing with non-toxic water-based coatings; a Basic Assessment under NEMA 2004 Listing Notice 1 may be required solely if the operation is located within a sensitive area or exceeds specified thresholds (e.g., site > 10 hectares).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero discharge of process wastewater to municipal sewers without written authorisation; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from coatings limited to applicable municipal by-laws and the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act; wood particulate dust controlled to a workplace permissible exposure limit of 1 mg/m3 for hardwoods; all solid waste transferred via registered waste transporters and hazardous waste classified under the Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the competent municipal fire authority; structural load inspection certificate for the manufacturing floor certified by a professional engineer; electrical certificate of compliance; occupational health and safety clearance from the Department of Employment and Labour confirming compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; machinery guarding and dust-extraction ventilation verification for all wood processing equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; customs clearance portal: eCleg at https://ecleg.sars.gov.za. SARS is the sole national tax and customs authority for income tax, VAT, customs and excise, with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) handling incorporation pre-registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned South African (Pty) Ltd: (1) incorporate with the CIPC, which immediately transmits a unique company registration number to SARS; (2) SARS automatically issues an income tax reference number to the new company; (3) the directors must activate the SARS eFiling profile and submit form RAV01 to register for VAT, PAYE, SDL, UIF and Customs Client status; (4) the company must appoint a public officer who is ordinarily resident in South Africa (Tax Administration Act 28/2011, s.26), failing which refunds and assessments are blocked; (5) VAT registration is compulsory once taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months (voluntary from ZAR 50,000). For a non-resident external company, the same RAV01 route is used after CIPC external company registration, supported by apostilled constitutional documents and proof of a local registered office; no court or ministerial approval is needed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South African law has no US-style check-the-box election: every incorporated (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxed at entity level at 27% corporate income tax on worldwide income (rates applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023). Statutory elections that remain available include: (i) voluntary VAT vendor registration under s.23(2) of VAT Act 89/1991 where taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000; (ii) VAT grouping election under s.50(1) for related companies of which one holds at least 80% shares; (iii) Headquarter Company election under s.9I of the Income Tax Act, requiring prior SARS approval and yielding exemption for foreign-held dividends, interest and royalties; (iv) CFC participation exemption elections under ss.9D and 10(1)(h) for outbound foreign dividends; and (v) deemed advance tax rulings are available to confirm zero-rating of export supplies. Hybrid mismatch instruments are instead subject to mandatory anti-hybrid disallowance rules (ss.8E, 8EA, 8F and 8FA), with no elective override.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory registration threshold in any consecutive 12-month period; ZAR 50,000 voluntary registration threshold; foreign suppliers of electronic services must register without regard to the threshold from their first month of exceeding ZAR 50,000 in annual taxable supply to South African recipients
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or API-based invoice stamping. VAT returns are filed electronically via SARS eFiling by the 25th day after the tax period; customs export declarations are cleared through the eCleg portal (SAD 500 declaration) with near-real-time electronic border release, but without an invoice-by-invoice government clearance. Tax invoices must meet the minimum content list in s.20(1) of the VAT Act and be issued within 21 days of the time of supply; s.9(1) applies the earlier of invoice date or payment date as time of supply. Since 2023, SARS promotes voluntary PEPPOL-compliant e-invoicing for procurement and business transactions; the scheme is available but not yet mandated, so no live fiscal stamp is required for exporting companies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under s.11(1)(a)-(e) of the VAT Act to the supply of movable goods (including Montessori beechwood blocks) where: (i) the supplier is a registered vendor; (ii) the goods are supplied to a non-resident (or to a resident for export under an export consignment); (iii) the goods are physically removed from South Africa within 90 days of the time of supply or within any written extension granted by SARS; (iv) the vendor retains prescribed proof of export; and (v) ownership in the goods passes to the recipient. Services are zero-rated only where physically rendered outside South Africa (s.11(2)(a)); services connected to the goods while in South Africa, or services rendered to residents, cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) submitted through SARS eCleg with the approved clearance/export entry number
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical removal of goods from South Africa to the non-resident customer's destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank-issued certificate of receipt of foreign currency evidencing collection of export proceeds within the SARB financial-surveillance deadline
Zero-rated VAT tax invoice bearing an export endorsement and containing all s.20(1) VAT Act content fields
Packing list, delivery note, freight and insurance documents evidencing delivery at the non-resident's address
Documentary proof of the recipient's non-resident status, such as export order, contract or foreign address records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS will restore output VAT at 15% on any supply for which the required export documentation is incomplete or false, and may retrospectively reassess all related periods under the normal-assessment rules. Consequences include: (i) additional VAT of 15% on the deemed local supply; (ii) fixed 10% penalty under s.39 of the VAT Act for default without reasonable excuse; (iii) behaviour-based understatement penalties of 0% to 125% of the shortfall under ss.222-223 of the Tax Administration Act 28/2011, with the 125% tier reserved for intentional tax evasion; (iv) interest at the prescribed rate under s.187 of the Tax Administration Act (currently repo rate + 3%); (v) denial of input credits and future refunds pending compliance; and (vi) criminal prosecution for fraud under the VAT Act and Tax Administration Act with fines and imprisonment of up to 10 years in aggravated cases. SARS operates a dedicated refund-verification unit that independently validates each export refund against customs data, banking records and shipping manifests before payment, and will claw back refunds paid if later found to be unsupported.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), in terms of the Currency and Exchanges Act, 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, administered through authorised dealers (commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is convertible for all current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, and for genuine dividend, interest, royalty and management fee remittances, subject to SARS tax clearance on the recipient and withholding tax to be effected at the South African source. Capital and financial account transactions, including inbound equity investment and cross-border shareholder loans, require reporting to FinSurv through an authorised dealer, but are generally approved provided the company is in good standing, the CIPC share register is up to date, and no prohibited funding source is involved. Profit distributions must observe the company's solvency and liquidity test under the Companies Act, 2008 and the Dividends Tax rate of 20% is imposed at source on shareholders; no general blocked-profit regime exists for bona fide non-resident shareholders. The main practical hurdle for remittance is the submission of the final dividend declaration, a solvency and liquidity certificate, and a SARB/SARS compliance confirmation to the paying bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in South Africa through an authorised dealer within 180 days from the date of shipment. Unless a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or retention allowance has been approved by FinSurv or the authorised dealer, all such proceeds must be surrendered into the South African banking system and credited to the exporter's account in rand. In substance, the mandatory conversion ratio is 100% for unauthorised non-FCA arrangements, whereas an FCA permits controlled retention of the export currency for subsequent approved trade payments. The exporter must submit the original customs export declaration and proof of receipt to the authorised dealer; failure to repatriate within 180 days constitutes an exchange-control offence and may result in administrative penalties, suspension of access to trade facilitation systems, and criminal liability under the Currency and Exchanges Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (FNB / RMB Private Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low, unless the EMI is a fully licenced South African bank or an authorised dealer in foreign exchange. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Mercury, or Payoneer cannot operate as the primary clearing rail for export proceeds because South African exchange control requires all trade receipts to be repatriated through an authorised dealer. They may be used only for ancillary pre-funding or marketing disbursements, never as the main revenue channel; routing export proceeds to an unrestricted offshore EMI would be viewed as a failure to repatriate and would trigger FinSurv penalties. Domestic digital adjuncts offered by licenced banks, including TymeBank as a licenced bank, may support retail-facing disbursement rails if they fully comply with FICA and use the bank's authorised-dealer framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA does not impose a universal in-person biometric requirement, but the AML/CFT framework requires banks to obtain comprehensive beneficial-ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, board resolutions, and corporate documentation. In practice tier-1 banks require at least one director and the financial signatory to attend a physical onboarding interview at the bank's offices for the first account, or to appear before a Commissioner of Oaths/notary who verifies identity documents and the company constitution. Remote onboarding is available for a South African registered proprietary limited company using digital identity verification, Home Affairs data-match, e-signatures, and a video interview, but the bank's KYC officer may still demand physical interviews where the shareholder structure is complex, where non-resident ownership exceeds 25%, or where any cross-border red flag is identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners controlling more than 25% of the proprietary limited company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners, a completed SARB Form B2 for foreign equity investment, a CIPC share register reflecting the issued shares, a board resolution accepting the non-resident capital contribution, an independent source-of-funds affidavit, and bank statements demonstrating the origin of the funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company registration or industry purpose flagged as a generic trading entity during new-account activation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC incorporation certificate, the Memorandum of Incorporation, a detailed business plan for the manufacture of eco-friendly beechwood Montessori blocks, the SARS tax reference number, import/export customs code, and the EN71/ASTM F963 laboratory test certificates for the finished toys.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hit on a director or major shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full passport copies, professional confirmations of PEP status if applicable, tax residency certificates, police clearance certificates from all citizenship and former residency jurisdictions, and a written narrative explaining the source of wealth and the absence of sanctioned relationships. Transaction-level corroboration by way of trading contracts and evidence of the physical goods itinerary is also required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction link or unexplained cross-border transaction patterns before the first trade disbursement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, bills of lading/house waybills, packing lists, letters of credit or SWIFT MT103 drafts, customs entry records, and a documentary 'know-your-customer' package containing directorship records, the ultimate decision-maker mandate, and the internal compliance sign-off for the specific transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Exchange-control authorisation is not required for a non-resident shareholder subscribing to ordinary shares in a South African proprietary limited company, but the authorised dealer must receive from the shareholder a completed non-resident declaration on SARB Form B2, together with the CIPC-allotted share certificate. The remitting bank must use a SWIFT MT103 with a clearly designated purpose code for direct investment, e.g. IMF Balance of Payments code for acquisition of equity capital in a South African resident enterprise. The inward funds are credited to a capital escrow account maintained by the authorised dealer; the company then allots shares within 30 days and files the return of allotment with CIPC. Any shareholder loan advanced separately must be evidenced by a formal loan agreement and reported on Form B1; the company's bankers must also verify that the capital injection does not pass through an unrestricted shell or personal wallet account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imported beechwood raw material and non-toxic finishes, use SWIFT MT103 payment orders for telegraphic-transfer settlement, denominated in USD or EUR, with the supplier invoice, customs entry, and bill of lading submitted to the paying bank. For higher-value or documentary trade, use irrevocable commercial letters of credit transmitted via SWIFT MT700, with payment against presentation of shipping, inspection, and compliance certificates (EN71, ASTM F963, and the certificate of origin). All outbound trade payments must be declared on the importer's exchange-control returns and reconciled against the company's export proceeds by the authorised dealer. Use of the bank's single-trade-transaction or supply-chain platform materially reduces document mismatch and preserves auditability for both the South African Revenue Service and SARB FinSurv.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) covering committed export proceeds and import payment obligations for a trade horizon of up to 12 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/ZAR, permitted only when the underlying is a real trade or loan exposure and when the authorised dealer confirms non-speculative purpose
Cross-currency swaps used to convert USD-denominated trade borrowings into ZAR, provided the exposure is supported by trade invoices and board approval

Currency options if the company adopts a board-approved hedging policy and obtains FinSurv-affiliated product approval; physically settled or cash-settled options may be used to hedge committed cash flows

Offsetting and unwind transactions that are strictly limited to closing a previously booked hedge on the same underlying exposure; speculative derivative trades are not permitted under South African exchange control

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act No. 71 of 2008, Section 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation or registration as reflected on the CIPC registration record.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late arrears attract escalating CIPC penalties and suspension of good standing; persistent non-filing for two or more consecutive years may lead to administrative deregistration or strike-off, with reinstatement requiring a court or CIPC restoration process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must accompany the annual return; any shareholding or beneficial ownership change must be filed within five business days of the transaction or event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the BO declaration is a criminal omission under the Companies Act; CIPC can issue compliance notices, impose administrative fines, and ultimately deregister the company for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory where the company's public interest score (PIS) equals or exceeds 350; a financial review by an external accountant is required when PIS is between 100 and 349; companies with PIS below 100 may prepare independently compiled financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); qualifying private companies may adopt IFRS for SMEs, with South African tax and Companies Act requirements remaining at entity level.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a complete Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office, file any change of beneficial shareholding with CIPC within 5 business days, and confirm the UBO schedule as part of the annual return. No annual separate UBO filing fee applies if submitted with the CIPC annual return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for earlier years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Corporation rates: 8% on first ZAR 95,750; 21% from ZAR 95,751 to ZAR 1,731,000; 27% above (if gross income below ZAR 20m and all shareholders are natural persons). Manufacturing allowances: s12B 40/40/20 on new manufacturing assets; s12C 40/20/20/20 on plant; s11D approved R&D deduction of 150% (phasing to 130%/110% after 1 Jan 2025); s12I industrial investment allowance 25%–35% on qualifying assets. Assessed losses: indefinitely carried forward under s20 Income Tax Act (the numeric schema field below records the 5-year convention used in the pipeline; South African law imposes no five-year expiry).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Companies and CCs Income Tax Return) filed electronically through SARS eFiling; provisional tax payments and returns declared on IRP6 via eFiling; a 10-digit company tax reference number is mandatory.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12-month financial year; year of assessment may end on any date, commonly 28/29 February).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14: within 12 months after the end of the company's year of assessment. Provisional tax: first IRP6 payment within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment; second payment on or before the last day of the year of assessment; voluntary top-up third payment within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, company registration number, SARS tax reference, eFiling PIN, financial year-end date, industry/sector code (3240), contact details and bank account information for refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert SARS-issued 10-digit tax reference for the ZA_PTY_LTD. Foreign-resident directors must have a SARS taxpayer reference (non-resident ITR) and should appoint a local SARS-accredited representative auditor/company secretary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 2: Statement of taxable income - Turnover/Sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from the sale of baby Montessori wooden blocks, reported net of VAT and less trade discounts, allowances and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in South African Rand (ZAR). E-commerce sales via Amazon Pay and Stripe must be translated at the SARS-approved spot exchange rate on the invoice/txn date; foreign warehouse dropshipping proceeds must be separately disclosed if title passes offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 2: Cost of sales & trading stock
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening stock, purchases of beechwood and non-toxic finishes, direct production labour, factory overheads, closing stock, and scrapping/adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer-priced inventory purchases from connected foreign suppliers must be arm's length; non-arm's length pricing triggers the s31(3) 100% adjustment without contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 2: Operating expenses and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, marketing, platform fees (Amazon, Stripe), salaries, depreciation, s12B allowances, professional fees, and other taxable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharge allocations from foreign head office must be supported by inurement-free, documented cost allocations; penalties for unsupported management fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior year and current-year loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restricted for companies where more than 50% of shares change within a 5-year window (s20A): a loss may not be set off unless the company remains in the same 'business of a similar nature'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after s20A set-off; normal tax at 27% (or SBC progressive rates); alternative minimum tax (s22B) not applicable to trading companies; dividend/royalty WHT credits not applicable to CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned Pty Ltd has no special rate; branch vs subsidiary status must be verified with SARS. A foreign parent cannot consolidate SA losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section 5: Provisional tax credits and refunds
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total IRP6 amounts paid (P1, P2, P3) and assessed tax decreases credited to the ITR14 assessment; the resulting amount is either tax due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company is a provisional taxpayer even when wholly foreign-owned; under-estimation by more than 20% triggers 10%–20% estimation penalties plus interest (s162 TAA).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: SARS administrative non-compliance penalties: fixed monthly charges from ZAR 250 to ZAR 16,000 per month (per outstanding return, capped at 35 penalty months); 10% late-payment charge on unpaid tax (s187 TAA); compounded interest at the prescribed rate (approximately 11.5%–12% per annum); understatement penalties from 10% (standard) to 150% (intentional tax evasion) (s223 TAA sched.); 100% transfer-pricing adjustment tax (s31(3)); criminal prosecution for persistent non-filing, bank/asset attachment, collection proceedings, and South African court judgments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividends tax imposed on the beneficial owner of the dividend (company must withhold and pay to SARS within 31 days of payment); no STC in the modern regime (secondary tax on companies abolished from 1 April 2012).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must complete the SARS 'Dividend Tax Treaty Rate' procedure: (i) obtain a valid foreign Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant treaty year; (ii) furnish the SARS-prescribed declaration that the shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend and holds the shares in substance; (iii) deliver these to the ZA_PTY_LTD before the dividend is paid; the company then applies the treaty rate (commonly 5% for corporate holders of at least 10%–20% of voting power, 10%–15% for portfolio holdings) and retains the documents for 5 years. If relief is not claimed at source, the shareholder must file a refund claim with SARS within 3 years, supported by the same TRC and a declaration. Article based on the principal DTAs in force (e.g., US-SA, UK-SA, Mauritius, Netherlands); gains on share disposals generally exempt in South Africa for non-residents if the disposal does not fall within deemed South African source property rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest 15% and royalties 15% (sections 49A–49H ITA), payable by the payer on amounts paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions (e.g., interest paid to a reporting institution, listed bonds, or a South African branch). Treaty relief: royalties commonly 0% under the US-SA DTA and 10% under several African/European DTAs; interest commonly 0%–10% depending on the DTA and LOB/PPT conditions; TRC + beneficial-ownership statement must be lodged before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold applies to the s31 connected-person rule; SARS administrative practice (Practice Note 7, 2023 TP Guide) uses ZAR 5,000,000 in annual cross-border connected transactions as the audit trigger for contemporaneous Local File documentation; a full Master File/Local File suite is expected where group consolidated revenue reaches ZAR 10 billion (CbC reporting threshold); smaller groups must still retain contemporaneous support for every connected transaction regardless of amount.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa enforces substance through four cumulative doctrines: (1) residence: central management and place of effective management (POEM) in South Africa makes the company tax-resident and fully taxable on worldwide income; (2) Controlled Foreign Company rules (s9D) attribute passive income of offshore subsidiaries to South African shareholders, with participation exemption for genuine active manufacturing income; (3) s31 TP rules require functional, asset and risk analysis, rejecting loosely priced cross-border flows lacking actual employees and value-adding functions; (4) GAAR (s80A-L) invalidates arrangements where the sole or main purpose is tax avoidance without a real business purpose. The ZA_PTY_LTD's onshore beechwood turning, warehousing, quality control, and Montessori certification workforce constitute adequate economic substance; a letterbox company holding only Amazon and Stripe accounts would fail the substance doctrine, be denied treaty benefits, trigger 20% dividends WHT re-characterization, and face CFC attribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating ZAR turnover from Amazon and Stripe rails, inflating purchase costs through connected shell suppliers, issuing false export invoices to remove taxable sales, or failing to register and file ITR14/IRP6.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 150% (intentional evasion) plus 100% additional tax on any TP adjustment; criminal conviction: fine equal to up to three times the tax amount evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years (s235 TAA; s104 Income Tax Act); interest runs from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and those controlling company finances are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax, penalties and interest if they knowingly failed to pay (s159, s179 TAA); SARS may obtain a personal tax judgment, a domestic travel ban/withdrawal of a passport, liquidation of personal assets, and, upon fraud findings, imprisonment of responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling wooden blocks to a foreign related distributor (or the Amazon corporate group via a connected reseller) at margins below arm's length, paying inflated management fees or royalties to a foreign parent, and failing to prepare or retain contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment by SARS to arm's length with 100% additional tax (s31(3) ITA), reduced to 50% only where adequate contemporaneous documentation exists; understatement penalty of 10%–150% may apply cumulatively; interest and 10% late-payment penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: False TP documentation exposes directors to s235 criminal liability for false statements and to s159 TAA personal liability for the additional tax; a director signing the IRP6 estimate based on a non-arm's length position may face an estimation penalty and personal claim by SARS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and abusive DTA/treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ZA (Pty) Ltd, or an intermediary foreign holding company, as a paper conduit with no local staff, premises, purchase order procedures or risk-bearing capital, solely to extract dividends or treaty-reduced royalties and interest; circular financing in the group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR voiding of the arrangement (s80A-L); re-characterization of distributions as dividends with 20% WHT; denial of dividend relief under LOB/PPT clauses; attribution of CFC passive income to South African shareholders under s9D; administrative penalties up to 150% plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for tax debts of a company that is a sham or facade (substance-over-form piercing), and for reckless trading under s77 Companies Act 71/2008, including civil restitution of amounts disbursed; SARS may seek freezing orders and residential/flexible travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain proper beneficial-ownership registers for the Pty Ltd, transacting with shell counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions, unexplained mismatches in export customs values versus Amazon-invoiced values, or cash structuring of imports of beechwood.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FIC Act administrative fines up to ZAR 100,000,000 for accountable institutions (and up to 15 years' imprisonment for natural persons for money laundering); SARS may also impose interpretations of criminal actions in respect of false trade documentation; forfeiture of the toys/equipment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers and company secretaries face personal fines under the FIC Act and potential imprisonment; directors' inability to demonstrate KYC/BO diligence creates criminal exposure and triggers cross-border travel restrictions while investigations are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file and pay / provisional under-estimation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the IRP6 due dates, filing the ITR14 beyond the 12-month window, basing provisional estimates on less than 80% of actual taxable income, or neglecting VAT registration once taxable turnover reaches ZAR 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monthly administrative penalties (ZAR 250–ZAR 16,000 per month per return, up to 35 months); 10% late-payment charge; estimation penalties of 10% or 20% of the difference (s162 TAA); prescribed-rate interest; SARS debt collection, instalment agreements requiring personal sureties, and forced liquidation of the Pty Ltd.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were aware of the company's failure to pay taxes are personally liable under s159 TAA for all unpaid tax and interest; shareholders who extracted dividends while VAT/PAYE/CIT were unpaid are jointly liable under the Companies Act dividend solvency test and may face claw-back actions by the liquidator.
